rationale: This is largely a mechanical re-specification of the archived ProductiveRDCapitalValue (same two legs, MUL swapped for SUMRANK plus industry demeaning), and industry-neutralizing is unlikely to explain or reverse that signal's negative FF5 alpha since the value leg is intangible-adjusted book-to-market whose alpha problem comes from factor loadings rather than sector tilts.

The construction is internally consistent (R&D is a genuine operating cash outflow, so adding it back does yield pre-investment cash generation, and both numerator and denominator are treated symmetrically for knowledge capital), and it is a substantively different cut from the archived expensed-R&D and EBITDA/EV variants rather than a cosmetic tweak.

The conditional logic is coherent and the expression matches the stated hypothesis with the correct natural sign, though the COALESCE(xrd,0) treatment collapses all non-R&D firms into a single tied middle rank on the conditioning leg, diluting the interaction into plain intangible-adjusted book-to-market for most of the cross-section.

This is essentially the product of two canonical published anomalies — R&D-to-market capitalization (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — so a positive result would be hard to distinguish from a mechanical blend of known factors rather than a new interaction.

This duplicates the archived IntangibleBurdenEVYield's denominator construction (market value plus reported intangibles) with EBITDA swapped for oancf and net debt dropped, and the denominator is economically incoherent since `intan` is an asset already reflected in market equity, not an additional claim, leaving the signal close to plain cash-flow-to-price.

Because `xad` is missing for most firms, COALESCE to zero makes DELTA(xad/sale) exactly zero for the large majority, so the second rank leg is a near-constant tie mass and the product degenerates into a rank of price-to-sales — i.e., a repackaging of the value anomaly (and of the archived RankedRDExpectationPremium structure whose alpha ran opposite to the expected sign).
